about: Missions to replay in Lunyx: real landing sites and time windows that play from the data bundled with the app, with no network and no credentials. Every window lies inside a bundled JPL Horizons table (public/data/horizons/index.json) and every site has bundled elevation data. Times are UTC. A test (src/data/presets.test.ts) checks this file against the catalogue, the bundled tables and the analysis.

presets.title: Blue Ghost Mission 1, Mare Crisium
presets.description: Touchdown on 2 March 2025, 08:34 UTC, then 14 days of daylight and the eclipse of 14 March.
sources: Site and touchdown time: the app's landing catalogue (public/data/landings.json): the lander's position measured in LROC images; touchdown 3:34 a.m. EST (NASA).
Sun and Earth: JPL Horizons (DE441), as seen from the site, no atmosphere; table bundled for 2025-03-01 to 2025-04-01.
Terrain: bundled elevation data for the site (LROC NAC model and SLDEM2015 windows, LOLA whole-Moon grid); the analysis lists the layers it used.

presets.title: IM-2 Athena, Mons Mouton
presets.description: Touchdown on 6 March 2025, 17:28 UTC, 5 degrees from the south pole: 14 days of low Sun, until it sets on 19 March.
sources: Site and touchdown time: the app's landing catalogue (public/data/landings.json): the lander's position measured in LROC images; the touchdown minute is not confirmed by an official source (NASA: about 11:30 a.m. CST, 17:30 UTC).
Sun and Earth: JPL Horizons (DE441), as seen from the site, no atmosphere; table bundled for 2025-03-05 to 2025-04-05.
Terrain: bundled LOLA south-polar elevation grids and the LOLA whole-Moon grid; the analysis lists the layers it used.

presets.title: Eclipse of 14 March 2025 at the Blue Ghost site
presets.description: Earth passes in front of the Sun, seen from Mare Crisium: partly covered from 05:00 UTC, hidden 06:17 to 08:34, clear at 09:51.

sunBehindEarth.reported: Reported for the lander (KUT Radio, 14 March 2025, citing Firefly Aerospace; local times read as CDT): eclipse from 05:00 to about 09:52 UTC, totality from 06:18 UTC. See docs/lunyx/validation.md.

sources: Sun and Earth: JPL Horizons (DE441), as seen from the site, no atmosphere; table bundled for 2025-03-01 to 2025-04-01. The times above are computed by the app from geometric discs (docs/lunyx/validation.md).

Earth in the sky is the app's model: its phase and the face it shows are computed, its picture is NASA's cloud-free Blue Marble. The thin ring around Earth while it hides the Sun stands for sunlight passing through Earth's air: it is drawn schematically, its brightness and colour are not computed.
Terrain: bundled elevation data for the site; the analysis lists the layers it used.
